articles.title: STAC3D Against the Odds: Characterizing the Musculoskeletal Phenotype of STAC3 Gene Disorder.
articles.authors: Adams NC, Choudhari M, Visco ZR, Vergun A, Stone J, Sanders JO, et al.
articles.population: Patients diagnosed with STAC3 Disorder (STAC3D), a rare genetic condition
articles.outcomes: Rates of musculoskeletal conditions including scoliosis (83%), hyperkyphosis (48%), joint contractures (61%), congenital foot deformities (61%), and need for orthopaedic procedures (57%)
articles.take_home: STAC3D is a rare genetic disorder commonly associated with spine curvature, clubfoot, stiff joints and short stature, affecting most patients and often requiring surgery. This study provides the first detailed picture of the musculoskeletal problems seen in STAC3D to help doctors recognise and manage the condition earlier.

articles.title: Trends in the management of type I and type II open forearm fractures in children.
articles.authors: Niknam K, Grellinger ED, Venishetty N, Swarup I
articles.population: Children aged 16 or younger with type I and II open forearm fractures
articles.outcomes: Infection rates and treatment costs between operative and nonoperative management
articles.take_home: Both operative and nonoperative treatment had similar infection rates (around 2%), but operative treatment cost nearly 4.5 times more than nonoperative treatment. The choice of treatment method did not change significantly over the 5-year study period.

articles.title: Establishing normative femoral morphology in the pediatric population using computed tomography.
articles.authors: Demirci B, Turhan Y, Yasar NE, Alkan H, Sezgin BS, Keceli AM, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective observational study establishing normative data
articles.outcomes: Femoral anteversion angle, intracanal diameter, and femoral antecurvatum measured on CT scans; comparison by age, gender, and side
articles.take_home: This study established normal measurements for thigh bone shape in growing children using CT scans. The study found that the angle of the thigh bone decreases with age, girls have different bone measurements than boys, and small differences between left and right legs are normal.

articles.title: Outcomes of Spinal Deformity Treatment in Asphyxiating Thoracic Dystrophy.
articles.authors: Kourpas KM, Stelzer JW, Jordan JV, Montgomery BK, Flynn JM, Cahill PJ, et al.
articles.population: Children with asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy (Jeune syndrome) treated with posterior spinal fusion for early-onset scoliosis
articles.outcomes: Operative time, blood loss, hospital and intensive care unit stay, and postoperative complications using modified Clavien-Dindo-Sink classification
articles.take_home: Children with asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy can safely undergo spinal fusion surgery to correct scoliosis, despite their lung problems and previous chest cage procedures. Most patients had short intensive care unit stays and manageable complications.

articles.title: Concurrent Validity of PROMIS-25 With PROMIS Pediatric Mobility in Pediatric Lower Extremity Trauma Patients.
articles.authors: Kelly N, Sang L, Coufal S, Swarup I
articles.population: Paediatric patients with surgically treated lower extremity trauma
articles.sample_size: 241 unique patients contributing 549 paired survey instances
articles.outcomes: Correlation between PROMIS-25 multidomain questionnaire (physical function, pain, fatigue, emotional health, social relationships) and PROMIS Pediatric Mobility questionnaire
articles.take_home: The PROMIS-25 questionnaire is valid for assessing recovery in children with lower limb trauma and provides more comprehensive information than the mobility-only questionnaire, without losing accuracy in measuring mobility itself.

articles.title: Oral step-down, optimal drug, and total duration of antibiotic treatment in African children hospitalised with severe community-acquired pneumonia (PediCAP): a factorial randomised controlled trial.
articles.authors: Bielicki JA, Clements M, Musiime V, Moore DP, Sidat M, Mulenga V, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 2 months to 6 years hospitalised with severe community-acquired pneumonia in sub-Saharan Africa
articles.sample_size: 1101 children randomised, 1055 with primary outcome data
articles.outcomes: Readmission or death at day 28; adverse events
articles.take_home: Switching children from intravenous to oral antibiotics (amoxicillin) after they improve clinically, with a total treatment duration of 4-5 days, works as well as the standard 5-day intravenous-only approach. Shorter total treatment durations were safe and non-inferior to longer courses.

articles.title: Selective Talonavicular Arthrodesis With Talocalcaneal Stabilization for Flexible Planovalgus in Cerebral Palsy: Outcomes Within a Pathophysiology-Based Treatment Strategy.
articles.authors: Badina A, de Remaurin XDC, Goudjo E, Georges S, Kerkouche A, Wicart P, et al.
articles.population: Ambulatory children with cerebral palsy and flexible planovalgus deformity with weak tibialis posterior muscle
articles.sample_size: 49 feet in 30 children, mean age 12.8 years
articles.outcomes: Walking distance improved significantly, walking ability on the Functional Mobility Scale improved at 500 metres, pain and shoe-wear difficulties decreased markedly, 83% family satisfaction, 12% unsatisfactory clinical outcomes, no fusion failures
articles.take_home: Selective talonavicular fusion with talocalcaneal stabilisation led to good medial column stability and improved walking distance in children with cerebral palsy and weak calf muscles. The procedure preserved walking ability and reduced pain, with high family satisfaction.

articles.title: A Pilot Study of the Wave Technique: A Safer, More Comfortable Approach to Pediatric Cast Removal.
articles.authors: Wang Z, Liu X, Zhu G, Hou N
articles.population: Children undergoing cast removal after elective orthopaedic surgery
articles.sample_size: 52 patients (28 Wave Technique, 24 conventional technique); 30 resident physicians for training assessment
articles.outcomes: Procedure time, procedural pain scores, parental satisfaction, skin injury incidence, resident training outcomes
articles.take_home: The Wave Technique for removing children's casts reduced procedure time by about 28 percent and pain scores by about 50 percent compared to traditional methods, whilst parents were much more satisfied and there were no serious complications in either group.

articles.title: Calcaneal Lengthening Osteotomy in Cerebral Palsy: Does Age at Intervention Influence Outcomes?
articles.authors: Westberry DE, Bailey JM, Shull ER, Layton BB, Hyer LC
articles.population: Children with cerebral palsy undergoing calcaneal lengthening osteotomy
articles.sample_size: 102 patients (155 feet), divided into cohorts: 55 patients (85 feet) aged 8 years or under, and 47 patients (70 feet) aged over 8 years
articles.outcomes: Radiographic correction of foot alignment, revision surgery rates, persistent pain, and pressure distribution in foot loading
articles.take_home: Calcaneal lengthening surgery for children with cerebral palsy works well and produces lasting correction whether performed before or after age 8. Younger age at surgery did not lead to more problems with correction failing or needing further surgery.

articles.title: Serial Casting Before Relapse Surgery: Investigating the Challenges of Relapsed Clubfoot Care.
articles.authors: Hay K, Gibson N, Knight D, Ng YX, Luo Z, Gibson M, et al.
articles.population: Children under 16 years with relapsed clubfoot treated surgically after initial Ponseti method management
articles.sample_size: 65 participants (14 received presurgical casting, 51 did not)
articles.outcomes: Number and complexity of surgical procedures required for relapsed clubfoot
articles.take_home: Children who received serial casting before surgery for relapsed clubfoot needed less complex surgical procedures than those who did not have casting. The casting group had a 40% reduction in surgical complexity compared with only 1.9% reduction in the noncasting group.

articles.title: The Hidden Injury: Behavioral Health's Role in Pediatric Orthopaedic Outcomes-A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Koshinski JL, Reikersdorfer KN, Pluhar EI, Cruz AI Jr, Seeley MA
articles.population: Children and adolescents with orthopaedic injuries and conditions
articles.outcomes: Role of psychological and psychiatric factors in orthopaedic recovery, return-to-sport outcomes, postoperative outcomes, and emotional distress
articles.take_home: Mental health problems in young athletes with bone and joint injuries are often ignored, but research shows that untreated anxiety and depression can slow recovery and delay return to sport. Adding psychology support to orthopaedic care, such as sports psychologists in clinics, may help young athletes recover better.

articles.title: Percutaneous tendon lengthening and selective percutaneous myofascial lengthening in children with cerebral palsy: Establishing surgical indications using the Delphi method.
articles.authors: Shrader MW, Shore BJ, Chambers HG, Theologis T, Kay RM, Rutz E, et al.
articles.population: Expert panel of 16 orthopaedic surgeons with at least 10 years' experience in cerebral palsy surgery
articles.sample_size: 16 panel members; 32 surgical indication statements surveyed
articles.outcomes: Consensus or general agreement achieved on 22 of 32 statements (69%). Consensus reached that percutaneous tendon lengthening for calf muscle (plantar flexor lengthening) should be avoided. Disagreement on 10 questions, mainly regarding need for more evidence comparing different percutaneous techniques.
articles.take_home: Expert surgeons agree that a minimally invasive percutaneous technique for lengthening the calf muscle in children with cerebral palsy should be avoided because of the risk of making it too long. More research is needed to determine when other percutaneous techniques are safe and effective.

articles.title: Radial nerve palsy following pediatric humeral shaft fractures: a systematic review and pooled analysis.
articles.authors: Metivier AJ, Callahan WT, Raju S
articles.population: Children aged 1-18 years with humeral shaft fractures and radial nerve palsy
articles.outcomes: Recovery of radial nerve function; associations between fracture type, treatment method, and nerve recovery
articles.take_home: Radial nerve injury after humeral shaft fracture in children is rare but more likely to have poor recovery when the fracture is oblique or located distally. Conservative treatment appeared to have better nerve outcomes than closed reduction and fixation, so careful early assessment of the nerve is recommended in these injuries.

articles.title: Impact of T4-L1-Hip Axis Normalization on Outcomes and Complications in Adult Spinal Deformity.
articles.authors: Mohanty S, Sardar ZM, Reyes JL, Hassan FM, Kelly MP, Coury JR, et al.
articles.population: Adults undergoing long-segment spinal fusion surgery for spinal deformity
articles.outcomes: Mechanical complications requiring reoperation (particularly implant failure and proximal junctional complications); patient-reported outcomes using Scoliosis Research Society and Oswestry Disability Index scores
articles.take_home: Keeping the spine's alignment balanced after fusion surgery reduces the need for further operations to fix implant problems, but achieving this balance did not improve patients' pain or disability scores compared to other outcomes.

articles.title: How Much Meniscal Translation Is Normal? A Pediatric Physiological Arthroscopic Meniscus Mobility Study.
articles.authors: Schultz CM, Lind DRG, Alayleh AM, Johnson BL, Tompkins MA, Schmitz MR, et al.
articles.population: Paediatric cadaveric knee specimens under 12 years of age
articles.outcomes: Normal meniscal translation percentages by location; meniscal rim width measurements; age-related variations in meniscal morphology
articles.take_home: The lateral meniscus is more mobile than the medial meniscus in children, with the lateral anterior horn showing up to 51.6% translation across the tibial plateau compared to 0-20% for the medial meniscus. Meniscal rim width increases with age, which may help surgeons decide how much tissue to remove when treating unstable menisci.

articles.title: Vitamin D Status and Screening Practices Among Pediatric Fracture Patients With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Retrospective Matched Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Murata A, Chehab M, Rajjoub R, Slyepkan I, Tulchin-Francis K, Tabaie S
articles.population: Paediatric patients treated for fractures, with and without autism spectrum disorder
articles.sample_size: 290 patients (145 with autism spectrum disorder, 145 without)
articles.outcomes: Vitamin D testing rates and prevalence of low vitamin D levels (insufficient <30 ng/mL and deficient <20 ng/mL); predictors of testing and low vitamin D
articles.take_home: More than half of the children tested had low vitamin D levels, and this was equally common in children with and without autism spectrum disorder. Children with autism were more likely to be tested for vitamin D, but socioeconomic disadvantage was a stronger predictor of low vitamin D than autism diagnosis.

articles.title: Provider-Cleared Return-to-Sport After Freiberg Infraction in Adolescent Athletes.
articles.authors: Touban BM, Amaral JZ, Chhabra BN, Miggins J, Kushare I
articles.population: Adolescent athletes aged 18 years or younger with symptomatic Freiberg infraction
articles.outcomes: Time to provider-cleared return-to-sport; proportion returning to sport with and without surgery
articles.take_home: Most adolescent athletes with Freiberg infraction (84%) returned to sport without needing surgery, typically within 3.7 months of starting treatment with a boot or cast. Those who eventually needed surgery took longer to return to sport, around 8.8 months.

articles.title: An Assessment of the Preoperative Vitamin D Levels in Patients Undergoing Limb Lengthening Surgery.
articles.authors: Yalcinkaya A, Yong B, Hatfield D, Bafor A, Iobst C
articles.population: Paediatric patients undergoing lower-extremity limb lengthening surgery for length discrepancy
articles.outcomes: Bone Healing Index, postoperative complication rates, association between baseline vitamin D status and bone healing
articles.take_home: Although low vitamin D was common in children undergoing limb lengthening (69% were deficient or insufficient), starting supplementation after surgery for low levels did not appear to affect bone healing or complication rates.

articles.title: Are Surgically Treated Long Bone Fractures in Adolescents Linked to Higher Rates of Substance Use Disorder? A Propensity-Matched Study.
articles.authors: Mittal MM, Acevedo KV, Tummala S, Pereira DE, Hosseinzadeh P
articles.population: Adolescents aged 14 to 17 years with surgically treated long-bone fractures of the upper or lower extremity
articles.sample_size: 24,249 with upper extremity fractures and 16,507 with lower extremity fractures, each matched with equal numbers of controls without fractures
articles.outcomes: Risk of developing substance use disorder within 2 years of fracture treatment
articles.take_home: Adolescents who had surgery for broken arm or leg bones were more likely to develop substance use disorder than similar young people without fractures, with lower-limb fractures carrying higher risk. This suggests a need for pain management approaches that avoid or minimise opioid use in recovering adolescents.
